name: Flatheads
tagline: Bengaluru sneaker brand, now owned by Styched
excerpt: Flatheads' founder turned down the only offer on Shark Tank India Season 2, sold out his stock after the episode, and the brand was later acquired by Styched.
content:
Flatheads made lightweight casual sneakers and sold them online. It was run by Ganesh Balakrishnan in Bengaluru, who had put his own savings into the company after his co-founder left.

He pitched in Shark Tank India Season 2, Episode 5, valuing the company at ₹25 crore. Aman Gupta said the basics of the business were not in place. Peyush Bansal and Vineeta Singh offered ₹75 lakh for about a third of the company, a valuation of roughly ₹2.25 crore. Balakrishnan declined, saying he needed to rethink his priorities. Anupam Mittal praised his honesty.

The episode struck a chord with viewers. Balakrishnan wrote on LinkedIn that the brand had almost sold out its inventory in India within days. In July 2023, the apparel brand Styched acquired Flatheads in an all-equity deal, and relaunched the label later that year.

Flatheads is a reminder that a no-deal episode can still change a company's fate.

shark_tank.pitch_summary: Ganesh Balakrishnan pitched his struggling sneaker brand at a ₹25 crore valuation. He declined Peyush Bansal and Vineeta Singh's offer of ₹75 lakh for about a third of the company.

faq.q: Did Flatheads get a deal on Shark Tank India?
faq.a: No. The founder declined Peyush Bansal and Vineeta Singh's offer of ₹75 lakh for about a third of the company.

faq.q: What happened to Flatheads after Shark Tank?
faq.a: Its stock sold out within days, and in July 2023 it was acquired by the apparel brand Styched.
The brand was relaunched by its new owner, Styched, in late 2023.
Ganesh Balakrishnan ran the company and pitched it on the show.

lessons: Honesty about a struggling business can win viewers even when it doesn't win investors.
A sold-out moment helps only if the company can restock; thin working capital limits what TV exposure can do.
An acquisition can be a good outcome for a brand that customers value but that lacks funding.
